group_assessment.counts_measured: Not measured as a publication count. The relevant measurement is that this is the Croce laboratory with Aqeilan as first author — the founding series of the gene — and that the paper cites its own group heavily: refs 4, 5, 6, 7 are Croce-lab papers, two of them 'in press' at submission (refs 6 and 7), i.e. uncheckable by a 2004 reader and only now resolvable.
group_assessment.weighting: OBSERVATION: the group that cloned and characterised WWOX is the group reporting its partners; four of the twenty-seven references are its own, two of which were unpublished at the time. INTERPRETATION, KEPT SEPARATE AND DECLARED AS SUCH: this is the ordinary condition of a founding series and is NOT a reason to discount the paper — parity of sources runs the other way, and the oncology origin is precisely why the mechanistic detail exists at all. It is a reason to weight the paper's INTERNAL evidence over its citations to itself, which is what this reading did: every finding below rests on a panel in this paper, not on a claim it inherits.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE ANSWER TO THE ASSIGNMENT'S QUESTION, AND IT IS NOT 'THEIRS' OR 'OURS' BUT A THIRD THING. CLAIM 023's four clauses are each FAITHFUL to this paper's abstract — I checked them one at a time against it. What is not faithful is the PROVENANCE: CLAIM 023 is `consolidated baseline`/`DATO` sourced to `CORPUS P206`, a registry record whose `Identifier` is the literal string `PENDING` and whose own note says `likely overlaps PAPER 026 (PMID 32185845); verify before merge`. PAPER 026 is ABSTRACT-ONLY and reports the OPPOSITE direction for the Tyr33 effect (phosphorylation DECREASES affinity for a p73-derived peptide). So the model has been carrying, as a datum, a correctly-worded summary of a paper nobody opened, attributed to a placeholder that names no paper, flagged as possibly the same record as an abstract that contradicts it. The content is right and the chain of custody is absent — which is worse than a misreading, because a misreading is visible.
entries.snippet: We have also demonstrated specific phosphorylation of Y33
entries.anchor: Discussion — the flat restatement, four paragraphs after the hedged one
entries.note: 🔴 ANCHORED IN THE DISCUSSION AND NOT IN THE ABSTRACT, ON PURPOSE AND AFTER THE VALIDATOR REFUSED THE ABSTRACT. The refusal improved the entry. The abstract's flat wording is what a reader downstream copies, but the Discussion shows the SAME hardening happening INSIDE the paper: `demonstrated` here, against `suggesting` in the Results section that describes the actual data. The loss of the modal is not something later readers did to this paper — it starts on page five of the paper itself, and the canonical claim is the fourth link in that chain, not the first.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE MODAL IS PRESENT EXACTLY ONCE, AT THE ONLY PLACE WHERE THE DATA ARE DESCRIBED. The Results hedge the phosphorylation finding with `suggesting`. The figure title drops it ('Phosphorylation of Wwox enhances its association with p73'). The abstract drops it. CLAIM 023 carries the flat form as `DATO`. Nobody falsified anything at any step; the hedge simply did not survive three transports, and the fourth turned the survivor into a datum.

entries.proposition: The 'several-fold' increase is quantified NOWHERE. Fig 4 is five blots with no graph, no error bar, no densitometry and no stated replicate count; the phrase rests on visual band comparison in a single panel.

entries.proposition: 🔴 FIG 4A IS NOT NORMALISED FOR THE AMOUNT OF p73 PRESENT, AND THE PANEL SHOWS WHY. The text compares lane 3 (Myc IP, DN-Src) with lane 6 (Myc IP, Act-Src) and lane 6 is indeed the stronger — that much the panel supports. But lane 4 (the anti-HA immunoprecipitate under Act-Src, i.e. the p73 recovery control) is grossly overloaded relative to lane 1 (anti-HA under DN-Src): a saturated black mass that bleeds below the 50 kDa marker, against a strong but contained band in lane 1. Fig 4B lanes 1 and 2 show the same asymmetry independently. MORE p73 WAS RECOVERED IN THE +Src ARM, so a stronger co-IP in lane 6 cannot be attributed to more association per unit p73. There is no input blot and no loading control in the panel. The direction of the effect survives; its magnitude and its cause do not.
entries.snippet: 293 cells were transfected with HA-p73β, Myc-Wwox, and Act-Src or DN-Src. Thirty-six hours later, whole-cell lysates were immunoprecipitated with anti-HA, anti-IgG, or anti-Myc.

entries.proposition: 🔴 FIG 4B DOES NOT SHOW WHAT THE TEXT SAYS IT SHOWS, AND THE AUTHORS DRAW A CONCLUSION FROM IT. The text states the level of phosphorylated p73 did not change between DN-Src and Src, citing lanes 6 and 8, and concludes p73 is not a Src target. In the panel, lane 8's P-p73 signal is visibly DARKER AND LARGER than lane 6's — they are not equal. FAIRNESS CUTS BOTH WAYS AND IS RECORDED: lane 8 is a Myc (Wwox) immunoprecipitate under +Src, so by the paper's own central claim it contains MORE co-precipitated p73, which would raise P-p73 signal at constant phosphorylation per molecule. There is no anti-HA reprobe of lanes 5-8 to normalise. So the panel neither establishes the equality the text asserts nor refutes the conclusion: IT CANNOT RESOLVE THE QUESTION EITHER WAY, and the text does not acknowledge that. The conclusion is under-determined by the figure it cites.
entries.snippet: Because the level of phosphorylated p73 did not change in cells with DN-Src or Src expression, we concluded that p73 is not a target of Src phosphorylation

entries.proposition: 🔴 FIG 4E SHOWS RESIDUAL Y33F PHOSPHORYLATION THAT THE TEXT DENIES WITH AN ABSOLUTE NEGATIVE. The text says WI-WT and WI-Y34F but NOT WI-Y33F and WI-Y33,34F could be phosphorylated. The panel at 7x shows a faint but present band for Y33F at 30 min, while Y33,34F at 30 min is genuinely blank. That pattern is internally consistent — a minor Y34 contribution revealed once Y33 is removed, abolished when both go — and it reads as Y33-major/Y34-minor rather than Y33-exclusive. The distinction matters because the Discussion elsewhere treats Y34 as dispensable outright.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE DISCUSSION CREDITS FIG 1G WITH AN EXPERIMENT FIG 1G DOES NOT CONTAIN. It states that Y34 and Y61 are dispensable for the interaction, citing Fig 1G. Fig 1G contains exactly three constructs — Wwox, WWY33R, WWY61R — verified by reading the panel headers at 7x. THERE IS NO Y34 CONSTRUCT IN ANY BINDING ASSAY IN THIS PAPER. WI-Y34F exists only in Fig 4E, the in-vitro kinase assay, which measures phosphorylation and not binding. The Y61 half of the sentence is supported; the Y34 half cites a panel that could not support it. Anyone transporting 'Y34 is dispensable for p73 binding' would be transporting an untested proposition with a figure number attached.

Its caption declares A, B and C only, and the image carries exactly three panels. The data meant are in Fig 3C. A dangling internal cross-reference, twice, in the paragraph that carries the paper's central interpretive move.

entries.proposition: 🔴 'SIGNIFICANTLY' IS USED WITH NO STATISTIC ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER, AND FIG 3A HAS NO ERROR BARS. The caption says the luciferase results are the average of three experiments; the panel shows twelve bars with ZERO dispersion indicators, while Fig 3C — from the same paper, same figure — does carry error bars and an explicit `average ± SD`. The screen over the whole body finds `P <`, `P =`, `P<` and `P=` at ZERO occurrences: no test, no threshold, no n per condition. The dose-dependence and the suppression are visible as a trend; 'significantly' is a word here, not a result.

entries.proposition: The pixel side, plus a second defect the text does not cause: Fig 3A carries no error bars on any of its twelve bars, and its y-axis is MISLABELLED. The axis reads `% of Luciferase (10³)` while the caption defines the values as fold induction over empty vector — and bar 1 is printed as 1.0, which is a fold and not a percentage. The printed bar values (1.0, 497, 1.7, 3.7, 2.7, 339, 63, 1481, 2062, 996, 303, 3366) are fold inductions on an axis claiming percent-times-a-thousand. Same class as the Z-score-printed-as-fold found in Liu 2018: a units label that would mislead anyone reading the panel without the caption.
entries.snippet: Results are shown as fold induction of the luciferase activity compared to control cells transfected with empty vector alone and are the average of three experiments.
entries.anchor: Fig 3A, y-axis label and twelve bars, inspected at native 462x747

entries.proposition: 🔴 COLOCALISATION IS ASSERTED WITHOUT A MERGED IMAGE, AND THE ASYMMETRY RUNS AGAINST THE CLAIM. Fig 2A shows each condition as two separate single-channel images side by side (c1/c2, d1/d2, e1/e2) — there is no overlay panel anywhere in Fig 2A, so 'colocalization' is inferred from two images and not shown in one. In Fig 2B the pattern inverts in the least helpful direction: the NEGATIVE conditions (i = p73γ, j = p73βY487A, k = p53) ARE displayed as two-colour merged images, while the POSITIVE ones (g = p73α, h = ΔNp73) are displayed as separate channels. The panels that would benefit most from an overlay are the ones that do not get one.

entries.proposition: THE ROUTING RESULT IS AN OVEREXPRESSION RESULT AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO IN THE DISCUSSION. This is the single most important qualification for a model that carries the routing principle as architecture: the redistribution of p73 is what OVEREXPRESSED Wwox does. The endogenous support is real but narrower — Fig 1B (etoposide-treated 293), Fig 1F and Fig 2B (MCF-7 endogenous Wwox), Fig 2C/D (siRNA knockdown) — and the endogenous localisation result is reported as 'more than 50% of MCF-7 cells' with no n and no test.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE DOSE-DEPENDENCE OF THE RELOCALISATION — THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE ROUTING EVIDENCE — IS IN A FIGURE THIS READING COULD NOT OPEN. Less Wwox giving more nuclear p73 is the closest thing in the paper to a causal titration, and it lives in supplementary Fig 5, behind PMC's proof-of-work. The claim is therefore carried here at the level the accessible panels support (Fig 2A, categorical, overexpression) and NOT at the level the text implies.

entries.proposition: THE Y33 RATIONALE IS INHERITED FROM A PAPER THIS CORPUS DOES NOT HOLD. Y33 was chosen for study because Chang et al. reported it affects murine Wox1's interaction with JNK; the same reference supplies the claim that altering Y33 reduces Wwox's proapoptotic activity. That reference is J Biol Chem 278:9195-9202 (2003) = PMID 12514174, already known to this corpus as MISSING FROM DISK AND UNREAD. PREMISE: DATO in the source, but a DATO we have never verified — the load-bearing premise under the whole Y33 story is a paper we do not have.
entries.snippet: Tyrosine 33 (Y33) located in the first WW domain was previously reported to affect the murine Wox1 interaction with JNK

entries.proposition: A NEGATIVE PANEL, AND IT IS TREATED AS ONE. The p53 non-interaction is a genuine and useful result — it is what makes the PPPPY-motif explanation specific rather than decorative — but Fig 1C is a negative panel and, per the standing correction, a negative panel does not by itself permit a comparison normalised for bait quantity. The authors' own framing is appropriately modal ('perhaps explaining'), and that modal is worth preserving on the way out.

entries.proposition: THE APOPTOSIS RESULT CONTAINS ITS OWN TENSION AND THE AUTHORS FLAG IT AS A GUESS. WWY33R does not bind p73, yet WWY33R + p73β gives the LARGEST apoptotic population in Fig 3C (~38%, above WT-Wwox + p73β at ~31%). The explanation offered is explicitly one possibility among others, not a demonstration. Anyone carrying 'Wwox-p73 cytoplasmic cooperation drives apoptosis' out of this paper must also carry the fact that the non-binding mutant produced more apoptosis than the binder.
entries.snippet: One possible explanation of this effect of WWY33R is that this mutation has a dominant negative effect on endogenous Wwox.

entries.proposition: A LABELLING HAZARD FOR ANYONE TRANSPORTING FIG 3C. The panel labels the amino-terminally truncated p73 isoform as `DN-p73`, while the same paper uses `DN-Src` to mean DOMINANT-NEGATIVE Src. In Fig 3C `DN-p73` means ΔNp73 — a deletion variant — not a dominant-negative construct, and the two senses of `DN` sit in adjacent figures. Recorded because the misreading is silent and would invert the interpretation of the ΔNp73 bars.
entries.snippet: ΔNp73 lacks the transactivation domain and possesses a dominant negative activity against p73, as well as p53

entries.note: The quoted sentence is what makes the collision genuinely confusing rather than merely notational: ΔNp73 IS described as having dominant-negative ACTIVITY, so `DN-p73` is defensible shorthand — and is still not the same thing as the `DN-Src` construct two figures away.

entries.proposition: Both p73 panels of Fig 5 contain BOTH morphologies, so the figure does not display the contrast the sentence draws from it. The high-Wwox field b2 contains a solid green ellipse whose centre-to-body brightness ratio is 1.10 (body mean 176.9, thirteen consecutive pixels at 193-199 across its middle) — indistinguishable from the nuclear p73 of the p73-alone control panel a, whose objects run 1.08-1.14. The reduced-Wwox field c2 contains a cell whose horizontal profile at row 61 runs bright-dark-bright (113 -> 54 -> 201), i.e. p73 EXCLUDED from the nuclear region. 🔴 METHOD NOTE, recorded because it governs how far this entry may be read: two independent automated segmentations of these panels disagreed with each other and with my own first visual impression, so NO directional claim is made about b versus c. What is established is the presence of both morphologies in both fields and the absence of any count that could weigh them.

entries.proposition: Fig 6 SUPPORTS the control it is cited for, and this is the reading's clearest positive finding about the supplement. At matched plasmid (1 µg) and matched p73β, the Wwox-to-tubulin density ratio of WT-Wwox versus WWY33R is 1.640 vs 1.503 at 0 ng p73β, 1.695 vs 1.217 at 10 ng and 1.827 vs 2.234 at 50 ng — WT/mutant ratios of 1.09, 1.39 and 0.82, straddling unity. The mutant is not systematically over- or under-expressed, so the Fig 3B result that WWY33R restores p21 is NOT obviously an expression artefact. ⚠️ My densitometry, not a reported result: the paper performs no densitometry, states no replicate count for this blot and prints no statistic on it.

entries.proposition: 🔴 STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISREAD AS AN ACCUSATION. The four Fig 7 panels with the LOWEST y-maxima (60, 60, 64, 72 — Wwox+p73β, WWY33R+p73β, ΔNp73+Wwox, Wwox) are exactly the four conditions Fig 3C reports as most apoptotic. That correlation is what GENUINE apoptosis would produce, because a depleted G1 peak lowers the auto-scale; it is recorded as a confound in the DISPLAY and explicitly NOT as evidence of manipulation. The consequence is only that the eye cannot be used here, and Fig 3C's own average ± SD from three experiments — which the caption does report — remains the quantification that carries the result.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE FINDING THAT NARROWS CLAIM 023, AND IT IS AN ABSENCE MADE MACHINE-CHECKABLE. The authors' own scope for the phosphorylation result is the INTERACTION, not the localisation: Y33 phosphorylation is said to regulate the Wwox–p73 interaction, and nothing more. Screened over the whole body from Abstract to Discussion, EIGHT sentences mention Src and ZERO of them also mention localisation, cytoplasm, nucleus, redistribution or sequestration. No experiment in this paper manipulates phosphorylation and measures where p73 goes: Fig 4 is entirely binding and phospho-blot biochemistry, while Fig 2 and Fig 5 are localisation with no Src arm. 'Phosphorylation-dependent subcellular rerouting' is therefore a CONJUNCTION of two separately supported legs and not a relation this paper tests.
entries.snippet: We have also demonstrated specific phosphorylation of Y33 ( Fig. 4 ), which regulate Wwox–p73 interaction

entries.proposition: The two Discussion sentences that carry the 'cytoplasmic cooperation drives apoptosis' leg BOTH cite a panel that does not exist. Fig 3's caption declares panels (A), (B) and (C) and the image carries three panels; the Discussion cites 'Fig. 3 D' twice, once for the ΔNp73 result and once for the increased apoptotic activity. The data meant are in Fig 3C, so this is a citation defect and not a missing experiment — but the leg of the argument that a downstream reader would follow terminates, twice, at a label with nothing behind it.
